product.quickSummary: Trilene Big Game is Berkley's heavy-duty nylon mono for anglers who want stretch, substantial line strength, and a large supply for respooling. Its diameter matters as much as its pound-test label: the selected size can be used as a working main line or as backing beneath another line.
product.suitabilitySummary: Big Game is worth considering for bait fishing, larger freshwater fish, and saltwater applications where nylon's stretch is useful. It also serves as economical backing. On smaller spinning reels, compare the actual diameter before choosing a heavy strength; a line can physically fit but still be awkward to cast.
product.chartNote: These entries match official US package listings to the same product codes in Berkley's diameter data. Only resolved strengths and package sizes are shown; the conflicting 25 lb listing is omitted.
strengthGuide: The 10 and 12 lb choices are the lighter entries in this chart. Check their diameters against the reel and lure you intend to use instead of assuming they handle like every other brand with the same strength label.

The 15 and 20 lb choices use more spool space and suit setups that can manage thicker nylon. A larger spool, heavier presentation, or bait-fishing application can make more sense than a small finesse spinning reel.

The 30-50 lb entries are substantial main lines. Choose them for a specific heavy-duty setup, not as a default upgrade for ordinary bass fishing. When Big Game is only backing, its diameter determines the length needed beneath your working line.

spoolingGuide.title: Big Game as the main line
spoolingGuide.text: For a full nylon spool, select your strength and use full-spool capacity. The large retail spool is a supply of line, not an instruction to put all of it on the reel.

spoolingGuide.title: Big Game as backing
spoolingGuide.text: This page calculates Big Game as the selected working line. To put Big Game underneath braid instead, open the braid's guide or the main calculator and select Big Game in the backing field.

spoolingGuide.title: Allow for stretch
spoolingGuide.text: Nylon's stretch changes how a rig feels compared with braid. Set the drag for the complete rod, line, and terminal setup; filling the reel does not establish a safe fighting drag.

faqs.question: Can Trilene Big Game be used for braid backing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the Big Game strength and diameter as the backing inputs, with your braid selected as the working main line. This page's calculator instead treats the selected Big Game as the main line.

faqs.question: Will a 1,500-yard spool fit on my reel?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a supply for several fills, not a single fill. The calculator estimates what your selected reel holds at the chosen diameter; stop at the reel's specified fill level.

faqs.question: Why is the 25 lb size absent from this chart?
faqs.answer: The available manufacturer diameter listing conflicts with neighboring strengths. That entry is withheld rather than used for a capacity calculation. This does not mean the product is unavailable.

product.quickSummary: 2020 US catalog reference, not a current-edition chart. These Trilene XT Clear filler-spool specifications come from Berkley's 2020 Product Guide. The guide records 4-30 lb options with lengths that change by strength; current formulation and availability are not established here.
product.suitabilityTitle: Planning around a documented XT spool
product.suitabilitySummary: XT is Berkley's abrasion-focused nylon monofilament. For a spool matching this historical reference, compare its printed diameter and model code before estimating capacity. The 10 lb entry is .014 in, so a reel marked for a different 10 lb line can hold a different amount. Do not apply this chart to unidentified older stock.
product.chartNote: Historical 2020 US manufacturer chart, printed page 236: Clear XTFS filler spools only. Inches are published; millimeters are converted at 25.4 mm per inch. Lengths are historical catalog offerings, not confirmation of current stock or edition. There is a 14 lb row, not a 15 lb row.
strengthGuide: At 4, 6, and 8 lb, the historical chart lists .008, .010, and .012 in respectively, each on a 330 yd filler spool. Check the reel's diameter-based capacity rather than assuming every 330 yd package is one reel fill.
The 10, 12, and 14 lb options use .014, .015, and .016 in line on 300 yd spools. Choose within the rod and lure ratings, then check how much that actual diameter leaves on your reel.
The 17, 20, 25, and 30 lb chart entries increase to .017, .018, .021, and .022 in. Package lengths step from 300 to 270, 250, and 220 yd; strength and package length must stay paired.
The later XTFS14-15 package photograph independently shows 14 lb, .016 in, and 300 yd. It supports that exact labelled package, not an assumption that the entire 2020 range is unchanged today.

spoolingGuide.title: Match the historical label first
spoolingGuide.text: Confirm Trilene XT, strength, diameter, and the XTFS model code on your own package. A modern product image identifies the family but does not date your spool or validate its condition.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep package length with strength
spoolingGuide.text: The archived 8 lb package contains 330 yd; the 10 lb package contains 300 yd. Plan working line and any backing from the selected diameter and the exact length printed on your package.

spoolingGuide.title: Condition matters with old stock
spoolingGuide.text: A catalog reference is not a statement that an old spool is fit to fish. Inspect stored line and test your knots before use; stop filling at the reel maker's specified level.

faqs.question: Are these current Trilene XT specifications?
faqs.answer: No. This is an explicitly historical 2020 US Clear filler-spool chart. Current product pages identify the family but omit numeric diameter metadata. The chart does not establish current formulation or stock.

faqs.question: Why does the archive address contain 2021?
faqs.answer: The hosting directory is named 2021_berkley, but the actual catalog cover says 2020 Product Guide and the page title identifies the 2020 catalog. The document itself determines the year.

faqs.question: Is the chart entry 14 lb or 15 lb?
faqs.answer: 14 lb. The manufacturer lists XTFS14-15, where the final -15 is part of the model code, not a 15 lb strength. No 15 lb entry is established by this source.

faqs.question: Why does 14 lb show .4064 mm rather than .40 or .41?
faqs.answer: The historical chart publishes .016 in only. Its metric value here is an explicit conversion. Separately pictured Berkley labels round their metric fields differently; those fields are not substituted into the historical chart.

faqs.question: Does a 300 yd filler spool mean my reel holds 300 yd?
faqs.answer: No. It is the packaged line length. Reel fill depends on the reel's spool capacity, actual line diameter, fill level, and any backing.

product.quickSummary: US package-label reference for 10, 15, and 20 lb Trilene 100% Fluorocarbon. The 10 lb evidence is a 2000 yd bulk spool; the 15 and 20 lb evidence is for 200 yd filler spools. These are exact pictured packages, not a complete strength range or a guarantee about every production run.
product.suitabilityTitle: Full-spool fluorocarbon or a measured working length?
product.suitabilitySummary: Berkley identifies this as 100% PVDF main line, distinct from fluorocarbon-coated nylon and its separate leader products. The verified 15 and 20 lb filler options are .015 and .017 in; check reel capacity before choosing them for a small spool. Backing can reserve the documented fluorocarbon for the working portion, provided the connection stays beyond the line you need to fish.
product.chartNote: US manufacturer-label evidence only: TF2010-15 at 10 lb/2000 yd, TLFFS15-15 at 15 lb/200 yd, and TLFFS20-15 at 20 lb/200 yd. Both diameter units are printed independently on each label. Other strengths and package combinations are intentionally omitted; these photographs do not establish stock availability.
strengthGuide: The documented 10 lb bulk spool is .012 in/.30 mm and contains 2000 yd. That is a bulk supply for planned fills, not an instruction to put the whole package on one reel.
The 15 lb filler label prints .015 in/.38 mm and 200 yd. Compare that diameter with the reel's rating when planning a baitcasting fill or a shorter working length over backing.
The 20 lb filler label prints .017 in/.43 mm and 200 yd. Its larger cross-section leaves less line on a given spool than the .015 in option; choose within the rod, lure, and reel requirements.
No numeric estimate is offered here for the remaining strengths simply because they appear in a store selector. The exact diameter and package must both be documented.

spoolingGuide.title: Separate bulk supply from reel fill
spoolingGuide.text: The 10 lb row documents 2000 yd, while the 15 and 20 lb rows document 200 yd. Measure each working length and keep the remaining line with its original strength and model identification.

spoolingGuide.title: Budget the working length
spoolingGuide.text: Leave enough fluorocarbon for casting, fish movement, and later trimming. When using backing, account for that working length before filling the remaining spool space.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep main line and leader identities separate
spoolingGuide.text: A short section used as a leader does not turn this product into Berkley's dedicated leader formulation. Do not substitute ProSpec, Vanish, Trilene XL Fluorocarbon, or a coated line's numbers into this chart.

faqs.question: Is this 100% fluorocarbon or coated nylon?
faqs.answer: Berkley specifies a proprietary 100% PVDF formula for Trilene 100% Fluorocarbon. This page is for that mainline product, not fluorocarbon-coated nylon.

faqs.question: Why are only 10, 15, and 20 lb included?
faqs.answer: Those are the strengths for which the inspected manufacturer package labels provide exact diameters and lengths. The current official selector lists more strengths but leaves diameter metadata blank.

faqs.question: Why is the 10 lb package 2000 yd?
faqs.answer: The verified photograph is the TF2010-15 bulk spool, SAP 1564072. A 200 yd filler package is a separate package identity and is not inferred from that bulk label.

faqs.question: Are the retailer diameter tables being used as the source?
faqs.answer: No. For 15 and 20 lb, the source is the manufacturer's printing on the actual spool pictured by the retailer. The printed model codes and SAP numbers match official Berkley US records.

faqs.question: Why do the inch and metric numbers not convert perfectly?
faqs.answer: Both are separately printed rounded label values. This chart preserves them; capacity calculations use the published inch diameter rather than replacing it with a conversion of the rounded metric field.

product.imageCaption: Vanish filler-spool package shown. The chart below covers verified bulk-spool specifications.
product.quickSummary: Berkley Vanish is a fluorocarbon main line designed with casting flexibility in mind. Its sinking material makes it a different choice from nylon for a working line. This guide uses the published US bulk-spool strength and diameter pairs, with capacity estimates based on the selected diameter.
product.suitabilitySummary: Vanish can suit subsurface presentations when you want a fluorocarbon working line without relying on a separate braid-to-leader connection. Lighter diameters are easier to manage on small spinning spools. The heavier entries need tackle that can handle thick fluorocarbon; they are not universal spinning-reel recommendations.
product.chartNote: The chart shows the resolved strength, diameter, and package combinations from Berkley's US Vanish bulk-spool listing. The 2,000- and 1,700-yard amounts are retail supplies, not recommended single-reel fills. Filler-spool and leader packages are not implied by this chart.
strengthGuide: The 6-10 lb entries are the lighter diameters shown here. Start with the rod's line rating, your lure, and the cover you fish. Filling a small spinning reel with fluorocarbon requires attention to line twist and the manufacturer's fill level.

The 12-20 lb choices give you a thicker working line for tackle and presentations that can manage it. For the same reel, increasing diameter reduces the available yardage; the calculator makes that tradeoff visible.

The 30-60 lb entries are heavy fluorocarbon choices. They are included because they have published specifications, not because they are recommended for everyday casting on every reel. A short leader and a full working spool are different jobs.

spoolingGuide.title: A supply spool is not a fill target
spoolingGuide.text: A bulk Vanish spool can supply multiple reel fills. Use the estimated full-spool amount as a starting point, then stop at the reel maker's fill level rather than trying to use the whole retail spool.

spoolingGuide.title: Replacing only the working section
spoolingGuide.text: Backing can let you replace a worn working section without discarding every yard on the spool. Leave enough usable Vanish above the backing connection for the casts and runs you expect.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the main line and leader distinct
spoolingGuide.text: This guide covers Vanish main line. A leader sold in a short spool should be checked against its own label, not assumed to share every diameter or package option shown here.

faqs.question: Is Vanish nylon with a fluorocarbon coating?
faqs.answer: No. Berkley describes this Vanish main line as 100% fluorocarbon. It should not be confused with a fluorocarbon-coated nylon or copolymer line.

faqs.question: Why does the package menu start at 2,000 yards?
faqs.answer: These are the bulk-spool packages whose strength and diameter combinations are documented in the source used for this chart. The calculator returns the amount for your reel, not the whole package.

faqs.question: Does a capacity estimate mean this strength is a good casting choice?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. The calculation estimates spool space. Match the line to the rod, lure, reel, and fishing conditions, especially with the thickest fluorocarbon sizes.

The chart uses the actual diameter printed on each package, not the separate mono-equivalent pound rating.
product.suitabilitySummary: Forward is positioned by Berkley for finesse presentations, including forward-facing-sonar fishing. The verified 10 and 12 lb packages are .007 and .008 in, so backing can be important when a 150 yd package is shorter than a reel's calculated full-spool amount. These are label-based capacity estimates, not measured casting, sink-rate, or abrasion comparisons.

strengthGuide: The 10 lb Low-Vis Green carton gives .007 in/.17 mm and 150 yd. Its additional 4 lb mono-equivalent text describes a comparison rating, not a 4 lb Forward strength.
The 12 lb Low-Vis Green and Flame Green spool labels give .008 in/.20 mm and 150 yd. Their 6 lb mono-equivalent text does not establish the diameter of the separate 6 lb Forward product.

Choose the required breaking strength within the rod and lure ratings, then use Forward's own printed diameter for capacity. Do not substitute the diameter of another braid carrying the same pound rating.
Treat these two verified strengths as a limited reference. No carrier count, PE rating, or numeric diameter for 6 or 8 lb is derived from the product name or retailer table.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan around 150 yards
spoolingGuide.text: A 150 yd filler package can leave unfilled space on a larger spool. Estimate backing using the working length you intend to keep, and stop at the reel maker's fill level.

spoolingGuide.title: Use the real diameter field
spoolingGuide.text: The .007 or .008 in printed diameter is the capacity input. The 4 or 6 lb mono-equivalent text is not an interchangeable line diameter and must not replace the 10 or 12 lb breaking-strength label.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the leader separate
spoolingGuide.text: Choose any leader for the presentation and contact conditions. Its strength does not change Forward's printed mainline diameter; leave enough main line that the backing connection remains beyond the fishing distance you need.

faqs.question: Is Forward a conventional X5 or X9 braid?
faqs.answer: No. Berkley describes Forward as longitudinally twisted and thermally fused. This source does not establish a conventional five- or nine-carrier count, and those other products' diameters are not substitutes.

faqs.question: Does 4 lb mono equivalent mean this is 4 lb Forward?
faqs.answer: No. The inspected carton is 10 lb Forward with .007 in/.17 mm diameter. The separate 4 lb mono-equivalent field is not its breaking strength. The 12 lb package similarly prints 6 lb mono equivalent.

faqs.question: Is the US filler spool 150 yards or 150 meters?
faqs.answer: The inspected US labels say 150 yd/137 m. A regional 150 m package is a different package identity and is not included here.

faqs.question: Why are 6 and 8 lb missing?
faqs.answer: The official US variants establish those products exist, but the inspected sources do not give a verified manufacturer diameter/package pairing for them. They remain outside this chart.

faqs.question: Will one filler spool fill my reel?
faqs.answer: That depends on the reel and selected diameter. When the estimated full-spool amount exceeds 150 yd, plan appropriate backing or a different documented line supply; a package length is not a reel-capacity rating.

features: Designed for optimal strength and casting distance
Smooth for long and quiet casts

product.quickSummary: Berkley X9 uses nine PE carriers and is positioned around a smooth casting feel. Choose the exact US pound-test label here, then compare its published diameter with your reel's capacity. The same brand's overseas strength labels are not automatically interchangeable with these entries.
product.suitabilitySummary: X9 is a candidate when a smooth braid main line and sensitivity are priorities. Its lighter sizes need careful spool tension and drag use; thin braid is not automatically the best choice for a baitcaster. Use the thicker options only when the presentation, cover, and tackle call for them.
product.chartNote: US strength and package options are matched by exact product code to Berkley's official diameter records. Inch diameters are published values; the millimeter figures are conversions. Retail lengths vary by strength, particularly in the heaviest sizes.
strengthGuide: The 8-15 lb entries are thin working lines. They can make sense on suitable spinning tackle with an appropriately chosen leader, but a fine diameter calls for careful knots, drag settings, and line management.

The 20-40 lb choices cover a wider range of applications. For baitcasting, choose the line around lure weight, cover, and resistance to digging into lower wraps rather than choosing only the highest capacity number.

The 50-100 lb options are for heavier uses that justify their strength and diameter. Compare both the amount your reel can hold and the package you intend to buy; not every large spool contains the same yardage at every strength.

spoolingGuide.title: Secure the braid at the arbor
spoolingGuide.text: Follow the reel maker's instructions for securing braid. Where backing is used, calculate its amount from its actual diameter instead of treating a mono pound test as a braid diameter.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep firm, even tension
spoolingGuide.text: Wind braid under controlled tension and watch the fill level. Loose lower wraps can change the usable fill and encourage the working line to dig in; the estimate cannot measure your winding tension.

spoolingGuide.title: Match the leader to the job
spoolingGuide.text: A leader is selected for the presentation, cover, knots, and target fish. Its pound test does not need to match the braid label, and changing a short leader does not produce a meaningful increase in spool capacity.

faqs.question: What is the difference between X9 and X5?
faqs.answer: X9 uses nine PE carriers; X5 uses five. Berkley emphasizes smooth casting for X9 and strength around cover for X5. Carrier count alone does not establish the capacity, knot strength, or abrasion performance of a particular spool.

faqs.question: Why do some imported X9 packages show different strengths?
faqs.answer: Regional labels can use different strength descriptions. This chart follows the matched US product codes and pound-test labels rather than mapping an overseas number to a US size by name alone.

faqs.question: Will the published diameter guarantee an exact fill?
faqs.answer: No. It provides a repeatable capacity input, but braid thickness, winding tension, and the reel's published capacity can affect the real fill. Stop at the reel manufacturer's fill level.

product.imageCaption: X5 Crystal package shown. The chart covers verified Low Vis Green product codes.
product.quickSummary: Berkley X5 is a five-carrier PE braid marketed for fishing around cover. The selected pound test identifies a specific catalog entry, while its published diameter drives the capacity estimate. Use this page to plan a full braid spool or a working section above backing.
product.suitabilitySummary: X5 can be considered for braid applications around vegetation and cover where the line strength, lure, and tackle are matched to the job. A cover-focused description does not make every X5 strength a heavy-cover recommendation. The lightest diameters still require a suitable reel and careful line handling.
product.chartNote: Strength and retail length are taken from US product options; diameters are matched using the same official product codes. Millimeter values are converted from the published inch diameter. Only resolved combinations are included.
strengthGuide: The 8-15 lb entries are the lightest choices shown. Treat them as fine braid, not heavy-cover line simply because the X5 family is marketed for cover. Check the rod and intended presentation before deciding on a strength.

The 20-40 lb entries span different diameters for general and stronger braid setups. A baitcaster may be easier to manage with a less delicate diameter, but lure weight, cover, and spool behavior should decide the choice.

The 50-80 lb entries belong to heavier applications that justify them. More breaking strength does not automatically improve casting or make a light rod suitable for dense cover. The capacity tool shows fit, not a blanket fishing recommendation.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose a useful working length
spoolingGuide.text: Plan enough braid for your normal casts, expected runs, and a reserve for cutting back damaged line. Backing can make up the remaining spool space without buying braid for the entire spool.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the connection
spoolingGuide.text: Use a connection appropriate to the braid and backing diameters, seat it carefully, and keep it below the normal working section. A tight, bulky knot can affect how the first braid wraps lie.

spoolingGuide.title: Inspect after contact
spoolingGuide.text: A cover-oriented braid still needs inspection. Check for damage after rubbing vegetation stems, wood, or rough structure, and cut back compromised line instead of relying on the strength label.

faqs.question: Is X5 a four-strand braid?
faqs.answer: No. Berkley describes X5 as a five-carrier PE braid. It is a different construction from its nine-carrier X9 model.

faqs.question: Does X5 hold less line than X9 at the same pound test?
faqs.answer: Use the listed diameters for the exact entries. Where two entries have the same diameter, the mathematical capacity estimate is the same; their construction or handling can still differ.

faqs.question: Can I put the whole 164-yard package on my reel?
faqs.answer: Only if your selected reel has enough estimated space at that diameter. Use a capacity calculation first, and stop at the correct fill level. If the package does not fill the reel, the backing mode can estimate what is needed beneath it.
